# swarmops check run

Run the checks of one stage of a clean workspace, or of a directory with --dir.

Runs the checks of STAGE (default before-land) that .swarmops/checks.toml names, or the one check default of .swarmops/workspaces.json's check.argv, or only the NAMEs given (each of the stage), one at a time in name order: each with no shell and no stdin, in its own process group, under its timeout\_s, in its dir. Every selected check runs, whatever an earlier one did, and one envelope names each outcome: passed, failed, timed\_out, not\_started, cancelled or not\_run. A run where any check did not pass is E\_CHECK\_FAILED, its details.run the whole result. A check gets the SWARMOPS\_CHECK\_\* variables, HOME, LANG, LC\_ALL, LC\_CTYPE, LOGNAME, PATH, TMPDIR, TZ and USER of your environment, and the variables --pass names; nothing else (the check default keeps your whole environment). Its output goes to a log with a time on every line, which check log reads. Once it has ended, the findings it wrote as JSON lines to SWARMOPS\_CHECK\_REPORT, and those of the JUnit and SARIF reports its definition declares that this run wrote, come with its outcome, at most 10,000 a run, the rest counted; they change no outcome.

The workspace form (--ws, --ws-path, else the workspace around the working directory) needs a clean workspace: no edits, not rebasing, not stale. It reads the check file from the store at the changeset the files stand for, holds the workspace's lock while the checks run, and never writes the store; its runs are kept in .swarmws/check-runs/. --dir DIR runs the checks of the files below DIR as they are, opens no store, and says vouched: its runs are kept below SWARMOPS\_CHECK\_RUNS\_DIR, else the state directory's swarmops/check-runs; the newest 20 of each are kept. SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP kill the running check's process group and end the run. No identity.

```yaml
title: "swarmops check run"
description: "Run the checks of one stage of a clean workspace, or of a directory with --dir."
group: "checks"
since: "0.13.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: false
mcp_tool: "check_run"
envelope_op: "check_run"
exit_codes: [0, 1]
errors: [E_CHECK_FAILED]
syntax: "swarmops check run [OPTIONS] [NAME]..."
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops check run [OPTIONS] [NAME]...
```

## Required arguments

None.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--ws`

Syntax: `--ws <NAME>`.

The workspace, by its name in the store's registry (default: the one around the working directory).

### `--ws-path`

Syntax: `--ws-path <DIR>`.

The workspace's directory.

### `--dir`

Syntax: `--dir <DIR>`.

Run the checks of the files below DIR on this host, as they are.

### `--stage`

Syntax: `--stage <STAGE>`.
Default: `before-land`.

The stage whose checks to run. Values: `before-land`: Before a change lands: the gate; `after-land`: After a change has landed; `scheduled`: On a schedule; `release`: Before a release is cut; `manual`: Only when someone asks for it; `deploy`: Before a deployment.

### `--pass`

Syntax: `--pass <NAME>...`.

A variable of your environment the checks also get; repeatable.

### `NAME`

Syntax: `<NAME>`.

Only these checks, each of the stage.

## Details

`check run` runs the checks of one stage that a tree's `.swarmops/checks.toml` names, one at a
time, and answers one envelope naming every check's outcome. It is how this repository's
maintainers and agents start the gate before a push: `so check run --dir . --stage before-land`.
The gate guides: the directory form is vouched for by the caller alone, and nothing records its
answer yet.

### Two forms

- **In a workspace**, `check run [NAME…]` with `--ws NAME`, `--ws-path DIR`, or the workspace
  around the working directory. The workspace must be clean: no edits on disk (`E_WS_DIRTY`, with
  the first 20 paths), not rebasing (`E_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICTS`), its base still on its target
  (`E_WS_STALE`). Its lock is taken (`E_WS_LOCKED` after a 5 s wait, retryable) and held until the
  run ends, so no `ws` command moves the files under a running check: a check that runs one gets
  `E_WS_LOCKED`. The check file is read from the store at the changeset the files stand for,
  never from the files on disk, and the result names that `changeset` and its root `tree`, the
  tree every check ran on; `vouched` is `false`. The store is only read: no writer lock is taken,
  and a check may write to the store itself. The runs are kept in the workspace's
  `.swarmws/check-runs/`.
- **In a directory**, `check run [NAME…] --dir DIR`: the checks of the files below `DIR` on this
  host, as they are, read as `check list --dir` reads them. It opens no store, so `--repo`,
  `SWARMOPS_REPO` and `--as` are not used, and the envelope has no `meta.repo`. The result says
  `vouched: true` and names no tree. The runs are kept below `SWARMOPS_CHECK_RUNS_DIR` (an
  absolute directory), else below the state directory's `swarmops/check-runs`
  (`$XDG_STATE_HOME`, `~/.local/state` or `~/Library/Application Support`), in a directory keyed
  by `DIR`'s canonical path, whose file `dir` names it. Nothing is written into `DIR`. Two runs of
  one directory at once are not kept apart.

### What runs

The checks whose `stages` hold `--stage` (default `before-land`), or of them only the `NAME`s
given, each run once, in name order. A name the file does not define is `E_INVALID_ARG` with
`details.reason: check`; a name not of the stage, `details.reason: stage` with the check's
`stages`; a stage with no check, or a tree with no check file and no `check.argv`, `no_checks`:
nothing runs then, so a gate that would run nothing fails. A file that does not read is
`E_CHECK_FILE`, as `check list` gives it.

Each check runs its `argv` with no shell and no stdin, in its `dir` below the root, in a process
group of its own, for at most its `timeout_s`; past it, the whole group is killed. However the
check ends, its group is killed once its output ends, or a second after it exits if a process it
left still holds the output: nothing it left running in its group outlives it. A check that
fails does not stop the run: every selected check runs. Outcomes:

| Outcome | When |
| --- | --- |
| `passed` | It exited 0. |
| `failed` | It exited with another code (`exit_code`), or a signal the runner did not send ended it (`signal`), or its log could not be written whole (a full disk, say): then `message` says why, whatever it exited with. |
| `timed_out` | It ran past `timeout_s`; its process group was killed. |
| `not_started` | Its `dir` is not a directory here (`not_started: dir`, as a sparse workspace may lack it), its program did not start (`not_started: program`, with the host's `message`), or its log or its own directory could not be made (`not_started: log`, with the host's `message`). |
| `cancelled` | A signal stopped the run while it ran; its process group was killed. |
| `not_run` | The run was stopped before it started: no process, no log. |

Only `passed` passes. Every check passed: the result, exit 0. Otherwise `E_CHECK_FAILED`, exit 1,
whose message names each check that did not pass and why, with the count of its findings when it
has any (`check failed (exit 101, 2 findings)`), whose `details.run` is the whole result below,
and whose hint names, for the first, where its findings are
(`details.run.checks[<i>].findings`) when it has any, then `check log`. A check that did not pass
carries the last 8 KiB of each of its streams (`stdout_tail`, `stderr_tail`); one that passed does
not.

### Findings

A check reports findings by writing them to its report file, the path `SWARMOPS_CHECK_REPORT`
names (in its own directory of the run, never in the tree; not made, so a check that has nothing
to report writes nothing). Once the check has ended and its process group is gone, the file is
read, and its findings come with its outcome: `findings`, `findings_total` and, in `reports`, the
file as it was read. It is read for `passed`, `failed` and `timed_out`; not for `cancelled`, whose
file a stop left partial. Findings change no outcome: a check that exits 0 passes whatever it
reports, and one that fails with none still fails.

The file is UTF-8, one JSON object a line, each line ended by `\n` (a `\r` before it is dropped,
and the last line needs none):

```json
{"level":"error","title":"unused variable `x`","path":"crates/app/src/lib.rs","line":12,"end_line":14,"message":"remove it, or start its name with _"}
```

| Key | Type | Required | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | string | yes | `error`, `warning` or `notice`. |
| `title` | string | yes | Not empty once trimmed. One line: a line break in it becomes a space. Cut to 200 bytes at a character's end, with `…`. |
| `message` | string | no | Cut to 4 KiB at a character's end, with `…`; line breaks kept. Left out when empty. |
| `path` | string | no | A repository path from the tree's root (the directory, in the directory form): no leading `/`, no `.` or `..`, at most 4 KiB. |
| `line` | integer | no | 1 to 2^32; only with `path`. |
| `end_line` | integer | no | From `line` to 2^32; only with `line`. |

A line of spaces and tabs alone is skipped. Any other line that is not a finding (not JSON, not
an object, a key not in the table, a missing `level` or `title`, a value of the wrong type or
outside its rule, more than 64 KiB, bytes that are not UTF-8) is skipped and counted in the
report's `invalid_lines`, and the report's `message` names the first one and why
(`line 3: unknown key "lvl"`). A file past 64 MiB is read to that bound, its last partial line
left out, and its report says `cut`. A report file that is a symbolic link, a FIFO or anything
but a regular file is `refused` with `fault: not_a_file`, and nothing behind it is read; one that
cannot be read is `refused` with `fault: io`. A report that is not read is never the run's error.

A run returns at most 10,000 findings and 4 MiB of their text (titles, groups, messages and paths
together), in run order: the checks in the order they ran, each check's in the order its report
gave them. From the finding that would pass either bound on, no finding of the run is returned,
but every one is counted: in its check's `findings_total`, its report's `findings`, and the run's
`findings_omitted`. The 10,001st finding of a run is counted and not returned. Each finding's
`report` is the index of its report in its check's `reports`.

### Reports a check declares

A check may also declare, with its `reports` key in `.swarmops/checks.toml` ([check
list](../commands/check-list.md)), the JUnit and SARIF files its tools leave in its tree. After the check
(for `passed`, `failed` and `timed_out`, as the report file), each is looked for at its `path`
below the check's `dir`, in declared order, after the report file, and read into findings:

| Format | A finding for | Level | Title | Group | Message | Path and lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `junit` | each `testcase` with a `failure` or `error` child | `error` | its `name` | its `classname`, else the nearest `testsuite`'s `name` | the first failure's `message` and text, then the end of the case's `system-err`, within 4 KiB | its `file` and `line` attributes, when it has them |
| `sarif` | each result whose `kind` is `fail` or not given | `error`, `warning`, `note` and `none` as `error`, `warning`, `notice`, `notice`; no level is `warning` | its `ruleId`, else its message's first line | its run's `tool.driver.name` | `message.text`, within 4 KiB | its first location: `artifactLocation.uri` (a relative reference, percent-decoded, or a `file:` URI below the check's directory) and `region`'s `startLine` and `endLine` |

A path is the report's, relative to the check's `dir`, joined to it to make a repository path from
the tree's root; one that is not a repository path then (absolute, `..`, another directory) is
left out, and the finding kept. A JUnit report's `reports` entry counts its cases (`tests`),
those that failed (`failed`, each a finding) and those skipped (`skipped`), as read, never as the
suites' own attributes say; a SARIF report's counts its `results`, of every kind.

Only a report this run wrote is read. Each declared path is looked at just before the check
starts, nothing read; after it, a report whose file is the same and unchanged (device, inode,
size, modification and status change times), or whose modification time is more than a second
before the check's start (a copy that kept an old time, say), is `stale`, and not read. `check
run` writes nothing in the tree it checks: a stale report is left where it is.

A report is opened from the check's directory one component at a time, never through a symbolic
link: a link anywhere below that directory, a directory, a FIFO or anything but a regular file is
`refused` with `fault: not_a_file`, and what it names is never read. Each report's `state`:

| State | When |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | Read: its `findings`, and its counts. |
| `missing` | Not there after the check. |
| `stale` | There, but not written by this run. |
| `refused` | There, and not read as its format: `fault` and a one-line `message` say why. |

| Fault | When |
| --- | --- |
| `too_large` | Past 64 MiB: nothing of it is read. |
| `not_a_file` | A symbolic link at any component, a directory, a FIFO or another kind of entry. |
| `not_text` | Not UTF-8: a UTF-16 byte order mark, or an XML declaration of another encoding, included. |
| `syntax` | Not XML or not JSON, cut short, or an entity reference other than XML's five. |
| `doctype` | An XML document type declaration, which could define entities: refused before anything is read. |
| `too_deep` | XML elements, or JSON arrays and objects, nested past 64. |
| `shape` | Well formed, but not the format: an XML root other than `testsuites` or `testsuite`; a SARIF log not of version `2.1.0`, without `runs`, or with a value of the wrong type. |
| `io` | It could not be read: the host's words in `message`. |

Nothing in a report is run, opened or followed: its paths are strings. Each report is read whole,
one at a time, at most 64 MiB of it, and of its findings at most as many as the run can still
return are kept. The JUnit and SARIF mappings may read more of a report in a later release; the
report file's format is the one this release fixes.

### Signals

SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP stop the run: the running check's process group is killed, that check
is `cancelled`, the checks after it are `not_run`, and the answer is `E_CHECK_FAILED` with
`details.run.cancelled: true`. A signal once the last check has exited stops nothing but what
that check left in its group: the run ends as its checks did. A second signal changes nothing.
A process that left its check's group, and a check left running when `swarmops` itself is killed
with SIGKILL, are not stopped.

### The environment

A check of `.swarmops/checks.toml` gets these variables, and of the caller's environment only
`HOME`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE`, `LOGNAME`, `PATH`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ` and `USER`, each when it is
set, and each `--pass NAME` that is set; nothing else. `inherited_env` lists the names given, never
their values.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_NAME` | The check's name. |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_STAGE` | The stage run. |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_TREE` | The tree's 64 hex digits in a workspace; empty in the directory form. |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_ATTEMPT` | `1`. |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_RUN` | The run's id. |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_REPORT` | The path of the check's report file of findings, JSON lines, not made; read after the check ends (see "Findings"). |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_OUTPUTS` | A path for the check's outputs, not made; nothing reads it yet (M31-6). |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_SUMMARY` | A path for the check's summary, not made; nothing reads it yet (M31-18). |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_ARTIFACTS` | A directory for the check's artifacts, made empty; nothing reads it yet (M36-3). |
| `SWARMOPS_CHECK_CHANGED` | Empty: no plan gives the changed paths yet (M30-4), so a check takes the whole tree as changed. |
| `SWARMOPS_WS` | The workspace's name, in the workspace form. |

A `--pass` name is 1 to 128 bytes of `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a `SWARMOPS_CHECK_` name nor
`SWARMOPS_WS`, at most 64 of them; another is `E_INVALID_ARG` with `details.reason: pass`.
The one check `default` of `.swarmops/workspaces.json` keeps the caller's whole environment, as
`ws land --check` gives it, with these variables set over it; `inherited_all` says so.

### The run and its logs

A run's `dir` holds `run.json` (its `state`, `running` then `ended`, and the `result`, the
checks' findings in it once they have ended), `lock`
(held while it runs), `logs/<check>.log` and `checks/<check>/`, the paths the environment names.
Each directory a run makes, the runs root and a directory's key directory among them, is its
owner's alone (mode `0700`), as a workspace's `.swarmws/` is: a log holds whatever its check
printed, secrets among them.

Each log holds both streams, a time on every line, and the sections a check opens; `check log`
reads one, and its page has the format. The newest 20 runs of a directory or a workspace are
kept, and a run whose lock is held, or cannot be tried, is never removed. A run of `--dir` also
removes the runs of each other directory that is gone (the `dir` file below their key names a
path that is not there), unless one of them is running: the runs root does not grow with every
throwaway directory checked. Nothing there is synced: the logs and records are diagnostics,
which nothing decides from. A log that cannot be written is its check's outcome, and the run goes
on; only a record that cannot be written makes the run `E_IO`, with the outcomes so far in
`details.run` and a hint naming the run's directory.

`duration_ms` is the run's, from its first check's start to its last's end, and each check's its
own; neither is a measured figure of any check.

### The MCP tool

`swarmops mcp` serves the workspace form as the tool `check_run`, whose arguments are
`CheckRunReq` (`workspace`, `stage`, `checks`), and whose result carries each check's findings as
the command's does: there is no directory form there, and no `--pass`,
since the server's environment is not the agent's to hand out; a check gets the fixed list of the
server's variables. A call holds the server until the run ends, each check bounded by its
timeout. SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP to the server stops the run as it stops `check run`: the call is
answered, and then the server exits. A check that did not pass makes the call's result an error,
`E_CHECK_FAILED`, with every outcome in `details.run`.

## Return information

`result` is a `CheckRunResp` (`swarmops schema CheckRunResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cancelled` | `boolean` | yes | Whether a signal stopped the run before its checks ended: the check running then is `cancelled`, those after it `not_run`. A signal once the last check has exited stops nothing: the run ends as its checks did. |
| `changeset` | `string or null` | no | The changeset the workspace's files stood for. Omitted in the directory form. |
| `checks` | `array of CheckRunOut` | yes | One per selected check, in the order they ran (by name). |
| `dir` | `string` | yes | The run's directory on the host it ran on, absolute: `run.json`, the logs and each check's own directory. |
| `duration_ms` | `integer` | yes | The run's milliseconds, from its first check's start to its last's end. |
| `failed` | `array of string` | yes | The checks that did not pass, in run order; empty when every one passed. |
| `file` | `string` | yes | The file the checks came from: `.swarmops/checks.toml`, or `.swarmops/workspaces.json` for the one check `default`. |
| `findings_omitted` | `integer` | no | The findings of the run that were counted and not returned: past the run's bound of 10,000 findings and 4 MiB of their text, every later finding is counted in its check's `findings_total` and here, and none is returned. Omitted when 0. |
| `inherited_all` | `boolean` | yes | Whether the checks got the caller's whole environment: only the check `default` of `.swarmops/workspaces.json`, which keeps what `ws land --check` gives it. |
| `inherited_env` | `array of string` | yes | The names of the caller's variables the checks got besides the pinned ones, sorted; no values. Empty when `inherited_all`. |
| `run` | `string` | yes | The run's id: a UUID v7, so that runs sort by their start. |
| `stage` | `CheckStage` | yes | The stage run. |
| `tree` | `string or null` | no | That changeset's root tree, 64 hex digits: the tree every check ran on. Omitted in the directory form, which knows no tree. |
| `version` | `integer or null` | no | The check file's `version`, 1. Omitted unless `file` is `.swarmops/checks.toml`. |
| `vouched` | `boolean` | yes | Whether only the caller stands behind the files the checks ran on: `true` in the directory form (`check run --dir`), which no gate accepts; `false` in a workspace, whose files were checked against `tree` first. |
| `workspace` | `string or null` | no | The workspace's name. Omitted in the directory form. |

Envelope `op`: `check_run`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.

## Errors

- [`E_CHECK_FAILED`](../errors.md#e_check_failed) (exit 1): A check failed or ran past its time: `ws land --check`'s or the bootstrap of `ws create` (`details.stage`: `check` or `bootstrap`; `exit_code`, `timed_out`, the tails of its output, `log`, `changeset`; nothing was landed), or one or more of `check run`'s (`details.run`: the run's whole result, every check's outcome and each check's findings, or `cancelled` after a signal).

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
